clue.text: Seafaring fellow embraced by girl

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it, so the girl's name wraps the fellow's

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name
Tim is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A sailor is hugged by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' is a crossword way to call for any man's name; here the short form of Timothy, held by 'embraced by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe matters connected with the sea and sailing.

clue.text: One's outwardly brave, for the most part

indicators.note: the brave word sits on the outside of the one, enclosing it

parts.note: manly means courageous
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is brave on the outside, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts MANLY round I; 's is 'has' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It means chiefly or largely, in the main.

clue.text: Soldier changes process of annulment

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a soldier in crosswords
changes are sequences rung on church bells, as is a peal

explanation.surface: A soldier alters the way a law is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' looks like a verb but is the bell-ringing noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoking an act of parliament is the formal undoing of a law.

clue.text: The will to install new mates in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the tent

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

indicators.note: new mates are mates made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to set up new friends in a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The will' reads as determination, but it is the legal document; 'new' shuffles and 'in' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is the legal document setting out a person's last wishes.

clue.text: Means of discovering hidden charges

parts.note: reads as a way to spot concealed fees, but the charges are buried explosives

explanation.surface: A tool for finding hidden fees on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: This device sweeps the ground to locate buried explosive mines.

clue.text: A fine concern to make a declaration

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a concern is a business, as is a firm

explanation.surface: Someone states a small business is doing fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something formally is to state it as true.

clue.text: It's enjoyable serving American mushrooms

parts.note: fun means enjoyable
a GI is an American soldier, a serving member of the US forces

explanation.surface: Serving mushrooms American-style is a pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms belong to the kingdom of spore-bearing organisms.

clue.text: Forced to use old measure in bar out East

indicators.note: the old measure goes inside what remains
with East out, that letter is dropped from the word for bar

parts.note: to impede is to bar or obstruct
an ell is an old unit of length for cloth

explanation.surface: Someone was compelled to use an old unit in an eastern bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a pub but is the verb to obstruct; 'out' drops the East letter and 'in' encloses the old measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven or compelled to act.

clue.text: Tory wet's way to assess for taxation?

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
to rate a property is to value it for local tax

explanation.surface: A soft Conservative's method of setting taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: A wet was a Thatcher-era term for a moderate Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Wets were the centrist members of the Conservative party, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Taking liberties and striking

explanation.surface: Someone presumptuous who also looks impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is presuming on others' good nature; the other is grand and impressive in appearance.

clue.text: Shot at bird observed by daughter

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone fires at a bird while their daughter watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed by' just places D after the bird, as if the girl is watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing from cover at a target is what a sniper does.

clue.text: Alienation of peculiar beings in SF film

indicators.note: the peculiar beings go in the film's title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's science fiction film
strange means peculiar
men are human beings

explanation.surface: An alien film features odd creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: The SF film is Spielberg's 1982 film about a stranded alien; 'in' wraps its two-letter title round the beings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state of becoming cut off or hostile, as between former friends.

clue.text: Woollen material a shopping area sent back

indicators.note: something sent back goes in the opposite direction, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct

explanation.surface: A shopping centre returns a woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns A MALL round to read LLAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric woven from the soft wool of the South American animal of that name is sold under the animal's name.

clue.text: He helps keep people's spirits up

definitions.text: He helps keep people's spirits up

parts.words: He helps keep people's spirits up
parts.note: reads as a cheerful friend, but spirits are strong drink, which this maker keeps supplied

explanation.surface: A cheerful friend lifts everyone's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as whisky and gin are produced by a maker who boils and condenses liquor.

clue.text: Leave hurriedly to attend a military entertainment

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
Beating Retreat is a ceremonial military display of drums and bands at sunset

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off to see a military tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Beating Retreat is a British military ceremony; BE AT A RETREAT means being present at one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to withdraw quickly from a place or position.

clue.text: Military coordinator's course of action an artist reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are said and heard

parts.note: a tack is a course of action; Titian was a Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A strategist's plan is relayed by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: TACK TITIAN said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in planning and directing military moves.

clue.text: Room over pub for typists needing a break

indicators.note: in a down clue the room sits over, above, the pub

parts.note: room means space
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Office typists take a break in a room above a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The long keyboard key inserts a gap between words.

clue.text: Parliamentarian's argument keeps mob leader in dungeon

indicators.note: the whole goes in the dungeon

parts.note: a cell is a prison room

indicators.note: the argument keeps the leader held inside it

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: the leader of mob is its first letter

explanation.surface: An MP in a dispute has a ringleader locked in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dungeon' gives the prison room; 'keeps' and 'in' build two containers, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell led the Parliamentary side in the English Civil War.

clue.text: City person foolishly involving church in brilliant display

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap round the church, taking it in
acting foolishly is acting without sense, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A City financier behaves foolishly at church during a spectacular show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles CITY PERSON and 'involving' sets CH among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireworks shows are the classic dazzling spectacle, and the word extends to any showy performance.

clue.text: Gymnastics group wanting a change in Spain

parts.note: PE, physical education, covers gymnastics
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A gym team wants to move to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' means small coins; the peseta was Spain's money before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's former currency unit, used for loose money.

clue.text: Roofs often are criticised like this

explanation.surface: Roofs often get a slating, i.e. a harsh review.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs are commonly covered in slate tiles, and to slate a play is to criticise it harshly.

clue.text: Officer keeping gold in chest of drawers

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it within

parts.note: a commode is an ornate chest of drawers
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An official stores gold in his bedroom furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest of drawers' wants to be a piece of anatomy, but it is the furniture; heraldic gold sits inside, signalled by 'keeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval officer ranking above captain holds this title.

clue.text: Nothing is as sheltered as this haven

indicators.note: the word as is sheltered by the other words around it

parts.note: O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: Nowhere is as protected as this refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing is as' reads as a comparison; 'sheltered' instead tucks the second word between the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert offers refuge from surroundings.

clue.text: Like theatrical husband or possibly beau

explanation.surface: A dashing stage husband, or perhaps a boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's play is An Ideal Husband; a beau ideal is a perfect model.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's play title gives the adjective for its husband, and the phrase beau ideal pairs the word with beau.

clue.text: Boldly confront monster crossing river

indicators.note: a monster crossing a river straddles it, so it holds the river inside

parts.note: a beast is a monster

explanation.surface: A hero faces a monster crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To face and push through something head on, as a swimmer does waves.

clue.text: Sorry to have to lock away one vintage wine

parts.note: to pen is to shut up in an enclosure
I is the Roman numeral one
tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: Someone regrets locking up a fine old bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is a deep red wine from Spain, an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone feeling remorse for wrongdoing is contrite.

clue.text: A partiality for spicy stuff

explanation.surface: A liking for hot sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a great enjoyment of something and a tangy condiment such as chutney.

clue.text: Criterion for a popular song

explanation.surface: A benchmark for judging a hit tune.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a yardstick for judgment and a well-known song often performed.
